user.title: Belgian Electricity Prices
user.description: Pick your supplier and region. Energy and grid rates are fetched live from the supplier's own publication.

contract.title: Contract
contract.description: Pick your contract. The integration fetches its current rate sheet on every refresh.

data.ytd_from_contract_start: Bill the year-to-date from the contract start date

data_description.contract_start_date: The date your supply under this contract started. Your rate is then read off the card of that month instead of today's, for every supplier that archives its past cards, and on fixed, dynamic and monthly-indexed contracts alike. If the tariff card you signed is named for a different month, give that month in the field below. The signing_card attribute on the current_price sensor names the card the entry ended up on. Leave blank to always use the current card.
data_description.tariff_card_date: Any date in the month of the tariff card your contract is on. A fixed or dynamic contract is priced at the card in force when you signed, and switching supplier takes about a month, so that card is often named for the month before your supply started. energie.be prints it in the product name (Elektriciteit dynamisch particulier online 06/26). Leave blank and the month your supply started is used, which is right when you signed and started in the same month. Only the card lookup reads this: your year-to-date window and fees keep counting from the contract start date above.
data_description.contract_end_date: The date your contract ends. Exposed as a timestamp sensor so an automation can remind you to renew, and used by the rolling year cost to say how much of the year is still under this contract. It changes no billed rate.
data_description.ytd_from_contract_start: By default the year-to-date cost counts from 1 January, whoever supplied you then. Tick this to start it at the contract start date above instead, so the figure covers only this contract. Fees are pro-rated over the same window, and the value drops the first time it applies. Only affects the contract's first calendar year; from the next 1 January the two are the same.

signed_rate.title: Signing rate (optional)
signed_rate.description: Leave this step empty unless your contract confirmation states figures that differ from your supplier's published tariff card. Many offers, promotions sold through comparison sites among them, have a card of their own, which the integration already reads. Fill in only a figure your contract states: it replaces the card's value, and a box left empty keeps it. When your supplier archives past tariff cards, the card for your signing month fills the empty boxes; otherwise the current card does. The spot factor multiplies the market price in EUR/kWh and the base is in EUR/kWh, so a formula printed in c€/kWh on a Belpex in EUR/MWh has to be converted: (0.1068 × Belpex + 1.5) × 1.06 c€/kWh is a factor of 1.13208 and a base of 0.0159. Per-kWh values include VAT on a residential contract and exclude it on a professional contract and on Ecopower's cards; the yearly fee includes VAT.

meter.title: Meter type
meter.description: Single-rate meter (mono), dual-time meter (peak/off-peak), or smart meter for dynamic contracts. The exclusive-night circuit is only for a second entry covering a separate night-only meter: chosen here, it bills the whole entry at the night rate.

professional.title: Professional contract
professional.description: Professional tariff cards are published excluding VAT, and the federal excise is degressive by yearly volume. Two answers are needed to price them.

data_description.include_vat: Turn this off if your business deducts VAT: prices, fees and costs are then reported excluding it. Injection follows the same choice.
data_description.annual_consumption_kwh: Your yearly consumption. The excise is billed per tranche (20 000 and 50 000 kWh per year: each slice of the year at its own rate), and the comparison quotes use it too. Once a full year has been measured on your meters, the measurement is used instead; 0 uses the measurement, or 3500 kWh until there is one.

direct_debit.title: Direct debit
direct_debit.description: Some tariff cards price a household that pays by direct debit differently.

data_description.direct_debit: Only shown where the tariff card states a difference, and what it moves depends on the card. On Mega's products it is the welcome ristourne: four grant the whole of it to a direct-debit payer alone, the rest add a supplement. On EnergyVision Groene stroom (sold as Brusol in Brussels) it is the yearly standing charge instead: 250 EUR a year against 230 on its cards up to September 2026, which those months are still billed on; the October 2026 card no longer prints the reduction.

dso_tariff_mode.title: Distribution tariff (Wallonia)
dso_tariff_mode.description: How your DSO bills you for the network. 'Simple' / 'Bi-horaire' match the existing meter convention. 'Tarif Impact' uses the CWaPE 3-band hour-of-day rates (PIC 17-22, MEDIUM 7-11 + 22-1, ECO 1-7 + 11-17) and requires a smart meter.

connection_power.title: Connection power (Brussels)
connection_power.description: Your contractual connection power in kVA. Brussels bills a Brugel 'Obligations de Service Public' fee scaled by it, and above 13 kVA Sibelga's higher power term. Most homes are on 13 kVA or less; a 3x400 V / 25 A connection with a heat pump or a charger sits above it.

api_key.title: ENTSO-E API key
api_key.description: Required for this contract. Its energy price is set by the Belgian day-ahead market: per slot on a dynamic contract, or on the delivery month's average on a monthly-indexed one. Request one for free at transparency.entsoe.eu.

injection_api_key.title: ENTSO-E API key (optional)
injection_api_key.description: Optional. This contract indexes its energy price on the delivery month's (or quarter's) day-ahead mean, or its solar injection on the day-ahead spot, or both, which needs a free ENTSO-E key from transparency.entsoe.eu. Leave blank to skip; without a key a card that prints a monthly figure is billed on it, which is the previous month's (or quarter's), while a feed-in formula settled per slot stays uncredited and its price unavailable.

api_key_unreachable.title: ENTSO-E could not be reached
api_key_unreachable.description:
Your API key could not be verified because the ENTSO-E Transparency Platform is not answering right now. This does not mean the key is wrong: ENTSO-E has outages lasting a day or more, and during one there is no way to tell a good key from a bad one.

You can check again in a moment, or continue and let the key be verified on the first price refresh. If it turns out to be rejected, a repair notice will tell you so and you can correct it then.

capacity.title: Capacity tariff (Flanders)
capacity.description: Prefer your meter's own monthly peak sensor (DSMR 5B publishes "Maximum demand current month"), which is the quarter-hour peak Fluvius actually bills. A plain power sensor is sampled hourly and only approximates it. Or use a fixed value.

solar.title: Solar panels
solar.description: Inverter capacity in kVA and the regime that applies to your installation. The Walloon compensation regime is reserved for installations certified before 2024-01-01 and stays valid until 2030-12-31; new installations and Flemish smart meters are on the injection tariff.

data.double_flow_meter: Meter counts draw and injection apart

data_description.double_flow_meter: Walloon compensation regime only. Tick it for a double-flow or communicating meter: the network then bills distribution and transport on your gross draws instead of the prosumer tariff whenever that costs less. Leave it off for a meter that runs backwards.

meters.title: Energy meters (current year cost)
meters.description: Optional. Either point at the four day/night registers from your meter (preferred - exact from the start), or at single cumulative consumption / injection sensors (the integration reads kWh from HA's recorder and splits each past day's total into day/night via the bi-hourly schedule when needed). Each side - consumption, injection - is resolved independently; you can mix one side as registers and the other as a single total. When both wirings are filled for the same side, the day/night registers win while they report whole; the total stands in for a pair with a dead, frozen or late half, or halves reporting different periods. If you've already set up HA's Energy dashboard, the cumulative fields - and the day/night registers when a utility_meter helper splits the grid source into peak/offpeak (or jour/nuit, dag/nacht, piek/dal) tariffs - are pre-selected for you. When the dashboard lists more than one import (or export) meter, such as tariff 1 and tariff 2, that side's total is left blank, since one register is not the total. Anything pre-filled stays editable.

data.card_archive: Read past cards from the project's archive
data.ev_home_charging_rate: Publish the CREG home charging rate for a company car

data_description.day_consumption_kwh: Cumulative meter register in kWh, one that only ever climbs. A sensor that resets, such as a 'this year' total, is read right only if its state class is total_increasing or it publishes last_reset; any other fall reads as zero.
data_description.night_consumption_kwh: Cumulative meter register in kWh, one that only ever climbs. A sensor that resets, such as a 'this year' total, is read right only if its state class is total_increasing or it publishes last_reset; any other fall reads as zero.
data_description.day_injection_kwh: Cumulative meter register in kWh, one that only ever climbs. A sensor that resets, such as a 'this year' total, is read right only if its state class is total_increasing or it publishes last_reset; any other fall reads as zero.
data_description.night_injection_kwh: Cumulative meter register in kWh, one that only ever climbs. A sensor that resets, such as a 'this year' total, is read right only if its state class is total_increasing or it publishes last_reset; any other fall reads as zero.
data_description.consumption_kwh: Used for its side when that side's two registers are empty, and in place of a pair that goes dead, freezes or reports different periods: a meter with no day/night split, a clamp meter, or an inverter that reports a single total. Same rule, it must only ever climb.
data_description.injection_kwh: Used for its side when that side's two registers are empty, and in place of a pair that goes dead, freezes or reports different periods: a meter with no day/night split, a clamp meter, or an inverter that reports a single total. Same rule, it must only ever climb.
data_description.daily_compare: Off by default. Once a day, at a fixed time derived from this entry so installs do not all fetch at once, price every contract of your kind sold in your region and publish the yearly saving of the best one as a sensor. Most days this costs a handful of freshness checks, because tariff cards are republished about once a month.
data_description.card_archive: On by default. For a past month your supplier no longer publishes a card for, fetch the card this project's own archive stored for it: one small file per month from GitHub, naming only the supplier, contract, region and month. It also reads, once a day, the VAT rate the archived cards agree on, for the prices a card states without one, and it is where this project's reading of a card published as page images comes from, so a supplier publishing those (Ecofix since August 2026) has no prices with it off. When the current card cannot be read and no card is held, last month's card from the archive stands in. Switch it off to keep the integration from contacting GitHub; those months are then priced on the current card, and a VAT rate a card does not state is the last one read while it was on, or else 6% for a household and 21% on a professional contract.
data_description.ev_home_charging_rate: Off by default. For a company car charged at home: publish the most your employer may reimburse per kWh tax-free under the flat-rate method, for your region and the running quarter, as the SPF Finances sets it from the CREG's prices. Your employer may pay less, or reimburse your actual cost instead. Ticking it lets the integration read one small file from creg.be once a quarter.

custom_energy.title: Custom energy formula
custom_energy.description: Note: this is an expert option only for suppliers that publish NO public tariff card. If your supplier publishes one, please open an issue on GitHub asking for it to be added as a proper provider instead of using this, and the same if your supplier is already listed but the entry does not price your contract the way your card does (a formula locked to the month you signed, a row the parser misses): open an issue with your card so it can be fixed for everyone rather than rebuilt here. A hand-entered contract is a static snapshot with no live card refresh and no drift check, so the numbers only stay correct if you keep them up to date yourself. Enter your contract's commodity figures excluding VAT; the VAT rate on the taxes step grosses them up. For the dynamic and monthly-average modes the price is factor x index + base, the index (the live spot, or the delivery month's mean spot) and the base both in EUR/kWh. A formula printed in c€/kWh on a Belpex in EUR/MWh has to be converted: (0.1068 x Belpex + 1.5) c€/kWh is a factor of 1.068 and a base of 0.015. Example (Yuso dynamic): factor 1.0, base 0.02.

data.custom_energy_factor: Energy factor (multiplier on the index in EUR/kWh)

custom_injection.title: Custom injection formula
custom_injection.description: How your solar feed-in is paid. A flat rate is a fixed EUR/kWh credit; a formula is factor x index + base against the live spot (dynamic) or the monthly mean (monthly-average). The index and the base are both in EUR/kWh, and the base keeps its sign: a card's (0,07 x Belpex - 2) c€/kWh, on a Belpex in EUR/MWh, is a factor of 0.7 and a base of -0.02. Tick the floor if the contract guarantees the injection price is never negative. Tick 'weight injection by the solar profile' to weight the monthly injection mean by the Synergrid solar production profile (fetched live; an ex-ante forecast, so close to but not exactly the settled SPP value).

data.custom_injection_factor: Injection factor (multiplier on the index in EUR/kWh)
data.custom_injection_base: Injection base (EUR/kWh, negative for a deduction)
data.custom_injection_spp_weighted: Weight injection by the solar profile (SPP)

custom_dso.title: Grid (DSO) tariffs
custom_dso.description: Regulated grid costs, identical for every supplier on your DSO. Copy them from your bill or your DSO's tariff sheet, excluding VAT. Only distribution is required. Leave the day, night and band boxes blank if your tariff has no such split: blank bills the single distribution rate, while 0 bills none. Leave any other charge you don't pay at 0. The yearly box takes the data-management fee (databeheer) in Flanders, the fixed term (terme fixe) in Wallonia, which the Impact tariff does not bill, and the metering and fixed-term charges together in Brussels.

custom_tax.title: Taxes and levies
custom_tax.description: Regulated taxes and levies, excluding VAT. The VAT rate below grosses up energy, grid and taxes (injection stays VAT-exempt). Belgian residential VAT is 0.06; set 0 if you entered VAT-inclusive numbers everywhere.

data.custom_tax_regional_renewables: Green levy: GSC + WKK in Flanders, green-energy contribution in Wallonia and Brussels (EUR/kWh)
data.custom_tax_region_connection_fee: Walloon connection fee (redevance de raccordement, VAT-exempt, Wallonia only) (EUR/kWh)
data.custom_professional: Business contract: bill the federal excise and energy contribution above as typed

settlement.title: Settlement
settlement.description: How your supplier settles this contract. Tick the box only if your account is billed per quarter-hour, whether you chose that when you signed up or switched to it later.

data_description.quarter_hourly: Only shown where your supplier lets you choose. Frank Energie: off for the hourly prices its card prints, on if you switched your account to quarter-hourly prices in the app. Bolt: off for variable settlement, where your month is billed on the month's RLP-weighted average, on for dynamic settlement, where each quarter-hour is billed at its own Belpex price. The formula is the same either way, only the market price it reads changes.

abort.compare_no_alternative: No other supplier or contract is available in your region to compare against.

error.meter_sensor_reused: This sensor is already picked in another field. Each field needs its own meter, or its kWh are counted twice.
error.compensation_kva_missing: The Walloon prosumer tariff of the compensation regime is worked out from the inverter capacity: enter it in kVA.

abort.compare_no_alternative: No other supplier or contract is available in your region to compare against.
abort.compare_all_no_alternatives: No other contract of this kind is sold in your region, so there is nothing to rank. The one-off compare can still quote a different kind of contract.
abort.compare_all_unknown_contract: This entry's contract is no longer in the supplier's catalogue, so it cannot be placed against the others. Re-pick it under Edit settings first.
abort.compare_all_entry_reloading: The entry is still loading. Try again in a moment.
abort.no_switch_recorded: No supplier switch is recorded on this entry for this year.

error.empty_api_key: Enter your ENTSO-E token. This contract is priced on the day-ahead market, so it cannot be set up without one. Get it at transparency.entsoe.eu (My Account Settings -> Web API Security Token).

error.whatif_volumes_required: Quoting a different regime needs your yearly consumption and injection in kWh: this entry has no injection meter wired, so they cannot be read from your meters.
error.switch_date_outside_year: The switch date must fall between 2 January and today.
error.switch_date_before_last: The switch date must be after the last switch recorded this year.
error.switch_date_before_start: The switch date must be after the start date of the contract you are leaving.

menu_options.compare_all: Compare every contract of your kind (ranked)

switch.title: Record a supplier switch
switch.description: Changed supplier during the year? Enter the first day the new contract supplied you. Your current settings are kept as the contract you held until the day before, and the next steps set up the new one, starting from what you have now. The year-to-date cost then bills each contract on its own tariff cards for its own days. In Wallonia under the compensation regime, each contract nets its own injection, as the regulator rules for a switch during the year.

data.switch_date: First day with the new contract

data_description.switch_date: The day the new supplier started supplying, as on its welcome letter or on the old supplier's final bill. Between 2 January and today, and after any switch already recorded this year.

remove_switch.title: Remove the last supplier switch
remove_switch.description: This removes the switch recorded for {until}, when you left {supplier} - {contract}, and puts the entry back as it stood before that switch was recorded: {supplier} - {contract} becomes your current contract again, with the settings it had then, and anything changed since is undone, except the answer to a question added after the switch was recorded, which is kept. To correct a switch date, remove the switch, then record it again with the right date and pick the new contract again. Submit to remove it.

edit.title: Belgian Electricity Prices
edit.description: Pick your supplier and region. Energy and grid rates are fetched live from the supplier's own publication.

compare.title: Compare another supplier
compare.description: Pick a supplier to quote against. Region, DSO and peak stay the same as your current entry; the meter type (unless the contract needs a smart meter) and, on an entry with solar panels, the solar regime can be changed on a later step to quote a what-if. Both static and dynamic suppliers are listed, so you can quote across contract kinds.

compare_contract.title: Compare another supplier
compare_contract.description: Pick a contract from {supplier}. Both static and dynamic contracts are listed, so you can quote across contract kinds, and your own contract is listed too: pick it to ask what the same contract would cost with a different meter type or solar regime, where those steps are offered: the meter only on a contract that does not need a smart meter, the solar regime only on an entry with solar panels.

compare_meter.title: Compare another supplier
compare_meter.description: Meter type for the comparison. Defaults to your current entry's setting; change it to see what the bill would look like under a different billing mode (mono = single rate, bi = peak / off-peak).

compare_solar.title: Compare another supplier
compare_solar.description: Solar regime for this quote. Pick a different one to see what you would pay under another metering arrangement; the regime your entry uses is preselected. Unlike the meter type this applies to both sides, because the regime belongs to your grid connection and not to the supplier. Nothing is saved. The two volume fields appear when no injection meter is wired to this entry: a meter that runs backwards reports consumption already netted against injection, which is not what the injection tariff bills, so enter your gross yearly figures from your inverter app or your annual meter readout.

compare_api_key.title: Compare another supplier
compare_api_key.description: This comparison needs ENTSO-E day-ahead spot prices: a contract priced off the spot (a dynamic one per slot, a monthly-indexed one on the delivery month's mean), or, on the injection regime, a contract whose solar feed-in is priced off the spot. Paste an ENTSO-E API token so the spot prices can be fetched. The token is used only for this comparison and is not saved. Leave it blank to continue without one: a contract priced off the spot then gets no price, a feed-in credit that follows the spot per slot is left out, as the result notes, and one indexed on a monthly mean is priced at the figure the card prints. On a one-off quote, a token also credits a feed-in that follows the spot per slot, on a contract whose energy is not spot-priced, in the year-to-date figures when both suppliers keep an archive of past cards. The ranking's year-to-date column does not use the token, and neither does the yearly estimate of that feed-in credit: both read only the day-ahead prices this entry has collected with a key of its own.

compare_result.title: One-off quote

api_key_unreachable.description:
Your API key could not be verified because the ENTSO-E Transparency Platform is not answering right now. This does not mean the key is wrong: ENTSO-E has outages lasting a day or more, and during one there is no way to tell a good key from a bad one.

You can check again in a moment, or continue and let the key be verified on the first price refresh. If it turns out to be rejected, a repair notice will tell you so and you can correct it then.

capacity.title: Capacity tariff (Flanders)
capacity.description: Prefer your meter's own monthly peak sensor (DSMR 5B publishes "Maximum demand current month"), which is the quarter-hour peak Fluvius actually bills. A plain power sensor is sampled hourly and only approximates it. Or use a fixed value.

solar.title: Solar panels
solar.description: Inverter capacity in kVA and the regime that applies to your installation. The Walloon compensation regime is reserved for installations certified before 2024-01-01 and stays valid until 2030-12-31; new installations and Flemish smart meters are on the injection tariff.

data.double_flow_meter: Meter counts draw and injection apart

data_description.double_flow_meter: Walloon compensation regime only. Tick it for a double-flow or communicating meter: the network then bills distribution and transport on your gross draws instead of the prosumer tariff whenever that costs less. Leave it off for a meter that runs backwards.

meters.title: Energy meters (current year cost)
meters.description: Optional. Either point at the four day/night registers from your meter (preferred - exact from the start), or at single cumulative consumption / injection sensors (the integration reads kWh from HA's recorder and splits each past day's total into day/night via the bi-hourly schedule when needed). Each side - consumption, injection - is resolved independently; you can mix one side as registers and the other as a single total. When both wirings are filled for the same side, the day/night registers win while they report whole; the total stands in for a pair with a dead, frozen or late half, or halves reporting different periods. If you've already set up HA's Energy dashboard, the cumulative fields - and the day/night registers when a utility_meter helper splits the grid source into peak/offpeak (or jour/nuit, dag/nacht, piek/dal) tariffs - are pre-selected for you. When the dashboard lists more than one import (or export) meter, such as tariff 1 and tariff 2, that side's total is left blank, since one register is not the total. Anything pre-filled stays editable.

data.card_archive: Read past cards from the project's archive
data.ev_home_charging_rate: Publish the CREG home charging rate for a company car

data_description.day_consumption_kwh: Cumulative meter register in kWh, one that only ever climbs. A sensor that resets, such as a 'this year' total, is read right only if its state class is total_increasing or it publishes last_reset; any other fall reads as zero.
data_description.night_consumption_kwh: Cumulative meter register in kWh, one that only ever climbs. A sensor that resets, such as a 'this year' total, is read right only if its state class is total_increasing or it publishes last_reset; any other fall reads as zero.
data_description.day_injection_kwh: Cumulative meter register in kWh, one that only ever climbs. A sensor that resets, such as a 'this year' total, is read right only if its state class is total_increasing or it publishes last_reset; any other fall reads as zero.
data_description.night_injection_kwh: Cumulative meter register in kWh, one that only ever climbs. A sensor that resets, such as a 'this year' total, is read right only if its state class is total_increasing or it publishes last_reset; any other fall reads as zero.
data_description.consumption_kwh: Used for its side when that side's two registers are empty, and in place of a pair that goes dead, freezes or reports different periods: a meter with no day/night split, a clamp meter, or an inverter that reports a single total. Same rule, it must only ever climb.
data_description.injection_kwh: Used for its side when that side's two registers are empty, and in place of a pair that goes dead, freezes or reports different periods: a meter with no day/night split, a clamp meter, or an inverter that reports a single total. Same rule, it must only ever climb.
data_description.daily_compare: Off by default. Once a day, at a fixed time derived from this entry so installs do not all fetch at once, price every contract of your kind sold in your region and publish the yearly saving of the best one as a sensor. Most days this costs a handful of freshness checks, because tariff cards are republished about once a month.
data_description.card_archive: On by default. For a past month your supplier no longer publishes a card for, fetch the card this project's own archive stored for it: one small file per month from GitHub, naming only the supplier, contract, region and month. It also reads, once a day, the VAT rate the archived cards agree on, for the prices a card states without one, and it is where this project's reading of a card published as page images comes from, so a supplier publishing those (Ecofix since August 2026) has no prices with it off. When the current card cannot be read and no card is held, last month's card from the archive stands in. Switch it off to keep the integration from contacting GitHub; those months are then priced on the current card, and a VAT rate a card does not state is the last one read while it was on, or else 6% for a household and 21% on a professional contract.
data_description.ev_home_charging_rate: Off by default. For a company car charged at home: publish the most your employer may reimburse per kWh tax-free under the flat-rate method, for your region and the running quarter, as the SPF Finances sets it from the CREG's prices. Your employer may pay less, or reimburse your actual cost instead. Ticking it lets the integration read one small file from creg.be once a quarter.

custom_energy.title: Custom energy formula
custom_energy.description: Note: this is an expert option only for suppliers that publish NO public tariff card. If your supplier publishes one, please open an issue on GitHub asking for it to be added as a proper provider instead of using this, and the same if your supplier is already listed but the entry does not price your contract the way your card does (a formula locked to the month you signed, a row the parser misses): open an issue with your card so it can be fixed for everyone rather than rebuilt here. A hand-entered contract is a static snapshot with no live card refresh and no drift check, so the numbers only stay correct if you keep them up to date yourself. Enter your contract's commodity figures excluding VAT; the VAT rate on the taxes step grosses them up. For the dynamic and monthly-average modes the price is factor x index + base, the index (the live spot, or the delivery month's mean spot) and the base both in EUR/kWh. A formula printed in c€/kWh on a Belpex in EUR/MWh has to be converted: (0.1068 x Belpex + 1.5) c€/kWh is a factor of 1.068 and a base of 0.015. Example (Yuso dynamic): factor 1.0, base 0.02.

data.custom_energy_factor: Energy factor (multiplier on the index in EUR/kWh)

custom_injection.title: Custom injection formula
custom_injection.description: How your solar feed-in is paid. A flat rate is a fixed EUR/kWh credit; a formula is factor x index + base against the live spot (dynamic) or the monthly mean (monthly-average). The index and the base are both in EUR/kWh, and the base keeps its sign: a card's (0,07 x Belpex - 2) c€/kWh, on a Belpex in EUR/MWh, is a factor of 0.7 and a base of -0.02. Tick the floor if the contract guarantees the injection price is never negative. Tick 'weight injection by the solar profile' to weight the monthly injection mean by the Synergrid solar production profile (fetched live; an ex-ante forecast, so close to but not exactly the settled SPP value).

data.custom_injection_factor: Injection factor (multiplier on the index in EUR/kWh)
data.custom_injection_base: Injection base (EUR/kWh, negative for a deduction)
data.custom_injection_spp_weighted: Weight injection by the solar profile (SPP)

custom_dso.title: Grid (DSO) tariffs
custom_dso.description: Regulated grid costs, identical for every supplier on your DSO. Copy them from your bill or your DSO's tariff sheet, excluding VAT. Only distribution is required. Leave the day, night and band boxes blank if your tariff has no such split: blank bills the single distribution rate, while 0 bills none. Leave any other charge you don't pay at 0. The yearly box takes the data-management fee (databeheer) in Flanders, the fixed term (terme fixe) in Wallonia, which the Impact tariff does not bill, and the metering and fixed-term charges together in Brussels.

custom_tax.title: Taxes and levies
custom_tax.description: Regulated taxes and levies, excluding VAT. The VAT rate below grosses up energy, grid and taxes (injection stays VAT-exempt). Belgian residential VAT is 0.06; set 0 if you entered VAT-inclusive numbers everywhere.

data.custom_tax_regional_renewables: Green levy: GSC + WKK in Flanders, green-energy contribution in Wallonia and Brussels (EUR/kWh)
data.custom_tax_region_connection_fee: Walloon connection fee (redevance de raccordement, VAT-exempt, Wallonia only) (EUR/kWh)
data.custom_professional: Business contract: bill the federal excise and energy contribution above as typed

compare_all_result.title: Ranked alternatives

data.with_ytd: Also compute year-to-date (slower: fetches each past month's card)
data.refresh: Price it again now (takes about two minutes)

settlement.title: Settlement
settlement.description: How your supplier settles this contract. Tick the box only if your account is billed per quarter-hour, whether you chose that when you signed up or switched to it later.

data_description.quarter_hourly: Only shown where your supplier lets you choose. Frank Energie: off for the hourly prices its card prints, on if you switched your account to quarter-hourly prices in the app. Bolt: off for variable settlement, where your month is billed on the month's RLP-weighted average, on for dynamic settlement, where each quarter-hour is billed at its own Belpex price. The formula is the same either way, only the market price it reads changes.

Only shown where your supplier lets you choose. Frank Energie: off for the hourly prices its card prints, on if you switched your account to quarter-hourly prices in the app. Bolt: off for variable settlement, where your month is billed on the month's RLP-weighted average, on for dynamic settlement, where each quarter-hour is billed at its own Belpex price. The formula is the same either way, only the market price it reads changes.

progress.sweeping:
Priced {priced} of {total} contracts. The fastest cards are fetched first, so the slowest suppliers arrive last and a pause is one of them, not a stall.

{ranking}

options.impact: Tarif Impact (3 bands by hour of day)

options.injection: Injection tariff (post-2024 install or smart meter)

refresh.name: Refresh
refresh.description: Force every Belgian Electricity Prices entry to re-fetch its supplier snapshot, the month cards its year-to-date cost is billed on and today's ENTSO-E prices immediately, instead of waiting for the next refresh tick. This does not touch the cache of PAST hourly prices behind the year-to-date cost; use Clear price history for that.

clear_history.name: Clear price history
clear_history.description: Also discard the cached past hourly prices that the year-to-date cost replays, and re-fetch them. Off by default: it re-fetches every day since 1 January (or the contract start, if the entry bills from it) against a rate-limited endpoint. The days before that are not fetched again, so a feed-in credit that follows the spot price per slot drops out of the rolling year cost and the comparisons until a full year is held again. Use it when a year-to-date figure looks wrong in a way an ordinary refresh does not fix.

cheapest_window.name: Cheapest window
cheapest_window.description: Return the cheapest contiguous window of N hours in the upcoming price table.

duration_hours.name: Duration
duration_hours.description: Window length in hours, rounded to the nearest whole hour (a half rounds up). On a 15-minute contract the window may start on any quarter-hour boundary.

entry_id.name: Entry ID
entry_id.description: Optional. Without it the first loaded entry is used, so set it when you have more than one entry.

earliest_start.name: Earliest start
earliest_start.description: Optional. Truncated down to the start of its price slot (the hour, or the quarter on a 15-minute contract), so 14:30 still considers the 14:00 slot. Defaults to now.

latest_end.name: Latest end
latest_end.description: Optional. Defaults to the end of the cached price table.

most_expensive_window.name: Most expensive window
most_expensive_window.description: Return the most expensive contiguous window of N hours in the upcoming price table.

duration_hours.name: Duration
duration_hours.description: Window length in hours, rounded to the nearest whole hour (a half rounds up). On a 15-minute contract the window may start on any quarter-hour boundary.

entry_id.name: Entry ID
entry_id.description: Optional. Without it the first loaded entry is used, so set it when you have more than one entry.

earliest_start.name: Earliest start
earliest_start.description: Optional. Truncated down to the start of its price slot (the hour, or the quarter on a 15-minute contract), so 14:30 still considers the 14:00 slot. Defaults to now.

latest_end.name: Latest end
latest_end.description: Optional. Defaults to the end of the cached price table.

backfill_statistics.name: Backfill statistics
backfill_statistics.description: Populate the recorder's long-term statistics for this entry's price sensors and current_year_cost across a date range, so the Energy dashboard shows history that predates the entry's first live tick. The cost is only rebuilt inside the current year-to-date window (from 1 January, or the contract start date if the entry bills from it); a range ending on or before its start rebuilds the price sensors only.

entry_id.name: Entry ID
entry_id.description: Optional. Without it the first loaded entry is used, so set it when you have more than one entry.

start.name: Start
start.description: First hour to backfill. Defaults to the start of the year-to-date window: Jan 1 00:00 of the current local year, or the contract start date if the entry bills from it.

end.name: End
end.description: First hour NOT to backfill (exclusive). Defaults to the current hour. On or before the start of the year-to-date window, only the price sensors are rebuilt.

clear.name: Clear ENTIRE series before re-import
clear.description: Destructive: deletes every existing row of the target series (not just the requested range), then the re-import repopulates only the requested range. Use ONLY to re-run the whole year-to-date window; a window that starts after the end year's year-to-date start (Jan 1, or the contract start date if the entry bills from it) is rejected with clear on, unless the window ends on or before the current year-to-date start (the cost series is left out of both the wipe and the re-import there). For narrower windows, leave this off: the import upserts on (statistic_id, hour) and already overwrites the requested hours without touching anything outside the range.

not_enough_hours.message: Only {available} price slots are available in the requested window; need {needed}.

not_enough_contiguous_hours.message: The requested window has at most {available} consecutive price slots; need {needed}.

no_loaded_entry.message: No loaded Belgian Electricity Prices entry.

no_loaded_entry_with_id.message: No loaded Belgian Electricity Prices entry with id {entry_id}.

entry_reloading.message: The entry is reloading; try again in a moment.

price_table_empty.message: The price table is empty; refresh the entry first.

snapshot_not_loaded.message: The supplier snapshot is not loaded yet; refresh the entry first.

snapshot_stale.title: Tariff data for {supplier} ({contract}) is more than {days} days old
snapshot_stale.description: The integration could not refresh the tariff card from the supplier and is serving cached data older than {days} days. Last fetch error: {last_error}. Prices may no longer reflect what is actually billed. Try the be_electricity_prices.refresh service, check your network, or open an issue on GitHub if the problem persists.

extractor_failed.title: Could not parse the tariff card for {supplier} ({contract})
extractor_failed.description: The supplier extractor raised an error: {error}. If a card was parsed before, the integration keeps serving its prices, but they may no longer match what is actually billed; otherwise this entry's sensors stay unavailable until a fetch succeeds. This usually means the supplier changed the layout of its tariff PDF or HTML page; please open an issue on GitHub with the supplier and contract so the extractor can be updated.

extractor_unreachable.title: Could not reach the supplier for {supplier} ({contract})
extractor_unreachable.description: The integration could not download the tariff card after several attempts: {error}. If a card was parsed before, it keeps serving its prices; otherwise this entry's sensors stay unavailable until a fetch succeeds. This is usually a temporary network or CDN problem that clears on the next refresh; run the be_electricity_prices.refresh service or check your network if it keeps happening.

extractor_card_missing.title: The tariff card for {supplier} ({contract}) is not available
extractor_card_missing.description: The supplier's site answered that there is no tariff card at the address the integration reads: {error}. The supplier may not have published this month's card yet, may have withdrawn the product, or may have moved its cards. If a card was parsed before, the integration keeps serving its prices, but they may no longer match what is actually billed; otherwise this entry's sensors stay unavailable until a fetch succeeds. This card clears by itself once the tariff card can be fetched again. If it lasts more than a few days while the supplier still offers the product, please open an issue on GitHub with the supplier and contract so the extractor can be updated.

card_read_by_ocr.title: Prices for {supplier} are read from pictures of its card
card_read_by_ocr.description: {supplier} publishes its tariff card as page images with no text layer, so nothing can be read out of the document itself. These prices for {contract} come from the project's own reading of the card's pixels, done once a day and shared by every installation. It reads a figure as the one thing it can be or not at all, so what you see was read whole rather than guessed, but it is a reading, and worth checking against your card before you act on it. This card clears by itself once {supplier} publishes a readable card again.

extractor_unreadable_no_prices.title: No prices for {supplier}: its tariff card cannot be read
extractor_unreadable_no_prices.description: {supplier} publishes its tariff card as page images with no text layer, so the prices cannot be read from it, and this entry has no earlier card cached to fall back on. This one is not a bug in the integration and reporting it will not help: there is nothing in the document to read. Every sensor on this entry ({contract}) stays unavailable until {supplier} publishes a readable card again, or until this project's card archive files its own reading of this card, which it does once a day and which this entry reads while "Read past cards from the project's archive" is on. To get prices now, add an entry with the 'Expert: custom formula' supplier and type the values from your card in by hand. This card clears by itself when either happens.

extractor_unreadable.title: The tariff card for {supplier} can no longer be read
extractor_unreadable.description: {supplier} now publishes its tariff card as page images with no text layer, so the prices cannot be read from it. This one is not a bug in the integration and reporting it will not help: there is nothing in the document to read. This entry keeps serving the last prices it managed to parse ({contract}), and those drift further from your real bill every month the card is reissued. To stay accurate, either switch to another supplier, or add an entry with the 'Expert: custom formula' supplier and type the values from your card in by hand. This card clears by itself if {supplier} goes back to publishing readable cards, or once this project's card archive files its own reading of this card, which it does once a day and which this entry reads while "Read past cards from the project's archive" is on.

entsoe_auth_failed.title: ENTSO-E rejected the API key for {supplier} ({contract})
entsoe_auth_failed.description: transparency.entsoe.eu returned 401 for the configured API key: {error}. Edit the entry's options and replace the key with a fresh token from your transparency.entsoe.eu account (My Account Settings -> Web API Security Token). Until then nothing on this entry that follows the day-ahead market can be priced: on a dynamic or monthly-indexed contract its sensors are unavailable, and on a contract whose feed-in credit alone follows the market that credit is.

supplier_deprecated.title: {supplier} is transferring your contract to {successor} on {ends_on}
supplier_deprecated.description: {supplier} is leaving the residential energy market: your contract transfers automatically to {successor} on {ends_on}. Prices stay correct until {supplier} stops publishing its tariff card, so nothing is broken yet, but this entry will stop updating afterwards. Once {successor} has started supplying you, open this entry's options, choose 'Record a supplier switch', enter the first day {successor} supplied you, then select {successor} and the product named on the letter they sent you. That keeps {supplier}'s days priced on its own cards, whereas 'Edit settings' would price the whole year on {successor}'s. If that day was 1 January of this year or earlier, use 'Edit settings' instead. If the product is not in the list, this integration cannot price that product yet: the 'Expert: custom formula' supplier takes the figures off your card by hand in the meantime, and an issue on GitHub is how it gets covered properly.

supplier_deprecated_ended.title: {supplier} has transferred your contract to {successor}
supplier_deprecated_ended.description: {supplier} left the residential energy market on {ends_on} and your contract has transferred automatically to {successor}. It has stopped publishing a tariff card, so this entry can no longer update: it is still showing the last prices it read, and those are no longer what you are billed. To price your new contract, open this entry's options, choose 'Record a supplier switch', enter the first day {successor} supplied you, then select {successor} and the product named on the letter they sent you. That keeps {supplier}'s days priced on its own cards, whereas 'Edit settings' would price the whole year on {successor}'s. If that day was 1 January of this year or earlier, use 'Edit settings' instead. If the product is not in the list, this integration cannot price that product yet: the 'Expert: custom formula' supplier takes the figures off your card by hand in the meantime, and an issue on GitHub is how it gets covered properly.

supplier_deprecated_no_successor.title: {supplier} stops supplying residential energy on {ends_on}
supplier_deprecated_no_successor.description: {supplier} is leaving the residential energy market on {ends_on}. Prices stay correct until it stops publishing its tariff card, but this entry will stop updating afterwards. Your contract is being transferred to another supplier: check the letter they send you. Once the new supplier has started supplying you, choose 'Record a supplier switch' in this entry's options, enter the first day it supplied you, then select it. 'Edit settings' would price the whole year on the new supplier's cards, unless that day was 1 January of this year or earlier. If it is not in the list, this integration does not cover it in your region yet: please open an issue on GitHub.

supplier_deprecated_ended_no_successor.title: {supplier} has stopped supplying residential energy
supplier_deprecated_ended_no_successor.description: {supplier} left the residential energy market on {ends_on} and has stopped publishing a tariff card, so this entry can no longer update: it is still showing the last prices it read, and those are no longer what you are billed. Your contract has been transferred to another supplier: check the letter they sent you, then choose 'Record a supplier switch' in this entry's options, enter the first day the new supplier supplied you, and select it. 'Edit settings' would price the whole year on the new supplier's cards, unless that day was 1 January of this year or earlier. If it is not in the list, this integration does not cover it in your region yet: please open an issue on GitHub.

contract_withdrawn.title: {supplier} no longer sells {contract}
contract_withdrawn.description: {supplier} stopped offering {contract} on {since}. This entry keeps pricing on the last tariff card {supplier} published for it, which stays right for as long as your contract runs on those terms, but that card will not change again. If {supplier} moves you to another product, choose 'Record a supplier switch' in this entry's options, enter the first day of the new product, then select it. 'Edit settings' would price the whole year on the new product's cards, unless that day was 1 January of this year or earlier.

exclusive_night_rate_missing.title: {supplier} ({contract}) does not publish an exclusive-night distribution rate
exclusive_night_rate_missing.description:
Your entry is configured for a separate exclusive-night meter circuit, but the tariff card {supplier} publishes for {dso} carries no exclusive-night distribution rate and no off-peak rate either. The integration is billing that circuit at the normal day distribution rate, so the network part of its price is higher than what you are actually charged. The energy part is unaffected.

Nothing can be substituted automatically: the integration never stores a price in its own source, and copying the figure from another supplier's card would be a guess. Ask {supplier} to print the exclusive-night distribution column, or switch this entry to a supplier whose card publishes it.

impact_rates_missing.title: {supplier} ({contract}) does not publish Tarif Impact rates for {dso}
impact_rates_missing.description:
This entry is set to the Wallonia Tarif Impact billing mode, but the tariff card {supplier} publishes for {contract} carries no PIC / MEDIUM / ECO distribution rates. The network part of the price falls back to the bi-hourly schedule while the energy part still follows the Impact bands, so the two disagree between 22:00 and 01:00, where Impact bills MEDIUM.

The bill stays close, but you are not being billed on the tariff you opted into. Switch this entry's DSO billing mode to bi-hourly, or pick a contract whose card publishes the Impact block.

connection_fee_missing.title: {supplier} ({contract}) no longer publishes the Walloon connection fee
connection_fee_missing.description:
Since the August 2026 card, {supplier} has stopped printing the "Redevance de raccordement" row on its Walloon tariff cards. Wallonia still levies this charge and the card's own terms keep taxes and network fees fully passed through, but the rate is published nowhere this integration can read.

Prices for this entry therefore exclude it, which under-bills by roughly 0,075 c€/kWh (about €2.60 per year at 3500 kWh). Everything else on the card, including the new flat federal excise, is priced normally. This notice clears automatically once {supplier} prints the row again.

prosumer_tariff_missing.title: {supplier} ({contract}) does not publish the {dso} prosumer tariff
prosumer_tariff_missing.description:
This entry is on the Walloon compensation regime, so the DSO levies a prosumer tariff per kVA of inverter. {supplier}'s card for {contract} prints its own photovoltaic forfait but omits the "Tarif prosumer" column that its other cards carry, so the network half of the fee is published nowhere this integration can read.

Prices for this entry therefore exclude it. The tariff runs from about €81 to €99 per kVA per year across the Walloon network operators, so a 5 kVA inverter is under-billed by roughly €400 to €500 a year. Everything else on the card, including the supplier's own forfait, is priced normally. This notice clears automatically once {supplier} prints the column again.

compensation_kva_missing.title: No inverter capacity on this compensation entry ({supplier}, {contract})
compensation_kva_missing.description:
This entry is on the Walloon compensation regime, whose prosumer tariff is worked out from the inverter capacity, but its inverter capacity is 0. The prosumer fee is therefore left out of every cost this entry reports: about €81 to €99 per kVA per year depending on the network operator, so roughly €430 a year on a 5 kVA inverter. With a double-flow or communicating meter the network bills distribution and transport on the gross draws instead, capped at the prosumer fee plus the network charges on the net draws; the integration bills the lower of the two once the solar step says the meter counts draw and injection apart, and the cap needs the capacity too.

Edit the entry's options and enter the inverter capacity (kVA) on the solar step. This notice clears once it is set.

register_pair_incomplete.title: A meter of {supplier} ({contract}) stopped recording
register_pair_incomplete.description:
{entities} records nothing, or stopped recording while the other register of its day/night pair, or the meter on the other side (consumption or injection), carries on. A day the consumption meters do not all report is billed on neither side, so the running cost of this entry reads low; a day only an injection meter misses is billed without its feed-in, so the cost reads high. No other error says so. A register that started long after its twin, as one rewired after a replacement does, bills the pair only from its first day, so this notice stays until the pair covers most of the year, unless a totals sensor wired on that side bills it instead.

Check that the sensor still exists and has a state_class of total_increasing; if it was renamed or replaced, point the Energy meters step at the new one. A sensor followed by a supplier and two dates belongs to a contract you held earlier in the year, which keeps the meters it had when the switch was recorded: to point it at another sensor, remove the supplier switch, correct the Energy meters step and record the switch again. This notice clears automatically once every meter reports again.

register_pair_covered.title: A register of {supplier} ({contract}) is broken
register_pair_covered.description:
{entities} records nothing, stopped recording while the other register of its day/night pair carries on, or no longer moves. The totals sensor wired on the same side is billing that side instead, so the running cost of this entry is unaffected.

The register is still worth fixing: check that the sensor still exists and has a state_class of total_increasing; if it was renamed or replaced, point the Energy meters step at the new one. This notice clears automatically once the register reports again.

direct_debit_unanswered.title: {supplier} ({contract}) prices direct debit and this entry has not been asked
direct_debit_unanswered.description:
The tariff card for {contract} prices a household that pays by direct debit differently: depending on the card, a direct-debit payer pays a lower standing charge, or receives a welcome credit, or a larger one.

This entry was set up before the question was asked, so no answer is stored and the difference is left out rather than guessed. Open the integration's options and answer "I pay by direct debit" to have it billed. This notice clears as soon as an answer of either value is stored.

brussels_power_term_missing.title: {supplier} ({contract}) is billed without Sibelga's power term
brussels_power_term_missing.description:
Sibelga's yearly fixed charge has two regulated parts, a metering one and a power one ("puissance mise a disposition"). The card for {contract} prints only the metering half, so the integration completes it from the figure Brugel publishes, and that sheet could not be read.

Prices for this entry therefore exclude the power part, which under-bills by about €50 a year. Everything else on the card is priced normally. The sheet is retried every six hours and this notice clears by itself as soon as it can be read.
